name: The tag-keeper's hands (narrator rig)
role: the unseen narrator's two steady hands, a mid-life teacher's (forties or fifties, never an old man's); the only part of him ever shown. They tie Promise Tags onto the copper line, flip them, re-tie tag 6 onto the wire of a as 'grid 1', place the marble, re-hang the line by dependency depth in the finale, and bend the last copper hinge into the viewer's hand

rig.entry: a fixed entry at the frame's lower left edge (the opposite side from the red-pencil hand, so the two never read as one person); forearms slide in on twos along a shallow arc and withdraw the same way
parts: right forearm + rolled linen sleeve + shirt cuff
handArt sprite per action (swapped, not morphed)
rig.rimLight: the backlight's warm rim on the upper edge of each cuff and knuckle; everything else ink

actions.tie: loop a tag's string over the copper line and pull a knot (lands on the detent's tie stroke)
actions.flip: turn a tag over with two fingers to show its back (lands on the flip stroke)
actions.place: set a marble, card or tag at a point (the marble at 4.5; the blank tag in the viewer's hand)
actions.lift: lift a tag off the line and re-hang it elsewhere (re-tying tag 6 on the wire of a; the finale's re-hang)
actions.bend: bend a short length of copper wire into a hinge, flat then up (ch04-s02, ch12-s06)
actions.holdUp: hold an object up into the backlight for the camera, then lower it

rig.rules: the narrator's hands never strike or write dissent: only the red-pencil hand does. No pointing at the audience, no tapping, no other gestures; anything else is staged as a variant of place, lift or holdUp with the same sprites

notes: Not a real person and never a likeness. No wedding band or jewellery, no age marks, no liver spots, no tremor; linen sleeve rolled once, distinct from the tweed cuffs used in another film. Puppet height is nominal: only forearms and hands are drawn.

signatureLock.module: reuse apps/bookshelf/src/viz/films/neural-net-history/sets/narratorHands.ts (copy it into this film's sets/ as narratorHands.ts): mirror HANDS_ENTRY to the lower left, swap the tweed sleeve and signet ring for a once-rolled linen sleeve and a bare hand; map tie and flip onto its pin/holdUp sprites, rivet onto stamp, lift onto unpinDrop, keep holdUp; add only bend and place as new actions

name: The red pencil (dissent)
role: a single anonymous paper hand holding a red pencil: the film's sign for doubt. It writes the dissenter's name and one word or number on a tag's back, strikes a broken belief through once, or rests beside a contested one. It stands for whoever the bible names as the dissenter; the name is always written as text, never given a body

rig.entry: always from frame right, a plain cuff, the pencil held in a pinch

actions.hover: approach a tag and stop at its edge without writing (ch01-s07)
actions.write: write a short name, word or number on a tag's back
actions.strike: one firm stroke through a tag's front (a dry scratch on the soundtrack)
actions.rest: lay the pencil on the line's post beside a contested tag and withdraw

rig.rules: the pencil is the only red in the film's frame (low chroma, emberRed rim); never held by the narrator's hands; never attached to a drawn face or body

notes: Generic and unnamed. Covers reviewers and readers too (the tutorial's test readers, the same-day review). Hacker News commenters get text cards only; this hand may carry their pencil mark onto a tag, but no figure is ever drawn for them.

does: rest (on the L6 post or the chapter's own post)
never: hold anything but the red pencil

name: Warren McCulloch
role: neurophysiologist and psychiatrist, Illinois Neuropsychiatric Institute; co-author of the 1943 logical calculus; ties on tag 1 (framing only)
notes: Appearance from the bible's secondary note (Gefter): full 'wild' beard, thin face, 1940s suit and tie, a cigarette. There is no cigarette prop in the kit: omit it rather than substitute a pipe. Confirm against licensed photographs before final art. Respectful profile; never caricature. Appears only in ch02.

name: Walter Pitts
role: self-taught logician in the University of Chicago circle; co-author of the 1943 paper (about twenty); ties on tag 1 beside McCulloch (framing only)
notes: Appearance from the bible's secondary note (Gefter): small, shy, bespectacled, long forehead (brow raised slightly, headScale y), the youngest in the room, a suit a touch too big. Confirm against licensed photographs before final art. Never caricature. Appears only in ch02.

name: Stephen C. Kleene (generic period figure)
role: logician at RAND, December 1951; finds part of the 1943 paper 'obscure', keeps the model, and recasts nerve nets as finite automata and regular events (framing only)
notes: Appearance not verified (bible §3): a deliberately generic 1950s academic in suit and tie, seen mostly from behind at a typewriter with the 98-page memo stacking beside him; never captioned as a portrait. His name appears as text on the red-pencil note and his knot card.

name: The clerk with a seating chart
role: a small paper-cut clerk, a teaching figure and not a person: in ch07 he assigns photos to rectangles before each training step (the learned gallery's min-cost assignment in plain JavaScript; the network learns where, JavaScript decides who); in ch09 two of him walk each 512-character JSON strip, backward then forward
notes: Generic and era-neutral in the paper-cut register (a clerk's sleeve garters, a clipboard as the seating chart). Drawn smaller than the human figures so he reads as part of the machine, not a historical person.

name: The viewer's open hand
role: an open, generic hand rising into the lower third in the last scene; the narrator's hands place the blank tag, tied to a copper hinge, into it: 'It's waiting for the next pair of hands.'

rig.entry: rises from the bottom edge, palm up (HandShape open), uncuffed: anyone's hand

actions.receive: the hand opens fully as the hinge and tag are placed, then holds still

notes: No sleeve, no ring, no age or gender signal: the audience's hand. Appears once.
